text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Wednesday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The major of Rokiskis in nothern Lithuania said three out of four judges in the city should be sacked for incompetence.
- Lithuania celebrates the 450th anniversary of the publication of the first Lithuanian book, the Katekizmas by Martynas Mazvydas.
- The health insurance medicine law which was due to come into force at the start of January is to be postponed for some four months by the government.

- The outgoing head of the statistics department forecasts that inflation in January may rise by up to 4.28 percent. The rise is due to the planned abolition of lower VAT rates on food items and fuel were abolished.
- Lithuania consumed 2.7 billion cubic metres of natural gas last year. It is 10 percent more than in 1995 but 2.2 percent less than in 1991.
- Mazeikiu Nafta refined 3.7 million tons of crude oil, 19 percent more than in 1995.
- The contraband vodka market in the country is 35 million litas, the head of the statistics department said.
- Consumers owed Lietuvos Energija 111.6 million litas for heating and 68.9 million litas for electricity at the beginning of 1997.
- The biggest Soviet-era daily Diena (former Tiesa) might face bankruptcy next Monday if nobody buys a control stake in it by Friday. The daily has not been issued since January 1.
- Three high ranking customs department officials resigned after state security officials arrested the head of the Kalvariju customs check point suspected of organising contraband.
- Poland will support the aim of Lithuania to join the European Union and NATO, said Polish Foreign Minister Dariusz Rosati after meeting Lithuanian counterpart Algirdas Saudargas.
